title: npub-cash v2
body:
This PR merges the long awaited second version of npubcash-server.

Features include
- Use mint quotes instead of proofs
- v2 API
- Removed Blink API (and the requirement for any Lightning backend at all)
- Multi Mint support
- Username purchase via Cashu 402
- Logging
- Rate Limits

title: migrated to monorepo
body: Moving from submodule pattern to a monorepo

title: Add support for user-selected mints
body: As of right now npubcash-server only works with a single mint that is defined by the service provider. This PR lets users choose their own mint and makes sure the server uses that mint to request ecash from.

title: Add text/identifier to lnurl response
body: This is needed for lightning address: https://github.com/lnurl/luds/blob/luds/16.md

title: Added strategy pattern for payment providers
body:
- Removed hardcoded payment logic
- Added a LightningHandler class that takes in a Payment Provider Instance
- Payment Provider Instances have to implement an interface

This allows us to add different payment providers along the go, without having to touch business logic. Simply add the Provider Class as module and switch out the Provider Instance in index.ts

title: Add NIP-57 Zaps to Cashu-Address
body:
Cashu-Address allows any nostr entity to receive eCash on their nostr public key via Lightning. The logical next step is for Cashu-Address to support nostr zaps, so that nostr users can receive Zaps directly in eCash. No setup required whatsoever.

This PR extends the LNURL part of the service to support NIP-57.

Issues to solve:
- NIP-57 currently required description_hash validation and Cashu mints do not support requesting a specific hash. Right now this is not an issue, as Cashu-Address uses Blink to proxy all invoices. However the roadmap includes dropping Blink and getting invoices directly from the mint.

title: New Claim Model + Database cleaner
body:
This PR introduces two fundamental changes to the Claim schema:

1. Claims are now mapped to a Transaction (Relational key constraint).
2. Claims now only hold a single Proof. If a Transaction includes multiple proofs, multiple claims will be created

The reason for this change is, that it makes it a lot easier to keep the database clean. This PR also includes logic to regularly (when user check their balance) check if tokens currently marked as "ready" are still unspent and updates their status if they are not. Claim route and balance route also no longer select ALL proofs but only those with status as "ready"

Log payment failures
body: Recent ddos attacks on mints have revealed some edge cases in which payments can fail. This PR is not a definite fix yet, but it makes sure failed payments do not go unnoticed.

This PR removes the requirement for env.HOSTNAME and replaces it wherever required with the value of the `host` header.

Open questions: Should a `validDomainList` be implemented to reject connections from unknown hosts in order to prevent NIP98 replay attacks?
